items.title: What interview skills training actually works, according to the research
items.pt:
In 2017, a team of researchers led from Northwestern University wrote that job interview training "is widely believed to be important for job seekers, which is seemingly common sense." Then they added the awkward part. A thorough literature review had turned up no previous study showing that better interviewing skills led to job offers. Their paper, published in Psychiatric Services, described itself as the first to confirm that link.

That gap is worth holding onto when you shop for interview s

items.title: Skills Section When Your Tools Are Obsolete: Write It Right
items.pt:
Why Empty Tool Names Hurt You More Than You Think


When a recruiter reads "Lotus Notes" or "Adobe Flash" on your resume, they do not mentally translate it into "email and document management" or "animation work". They pause and judge the age of your experience, a risk you do not want. A resume should prove what you can do today, not catalog everything you touched ten years ago. The fix is straightforward: you do not need to remove the experience; you just need to relabel it.

items.title: Telescopic Language Models
items.pt: One deployed language model must often serve many compute budgets, yet serving each budget still means a separate training or compression run per point. We train a Telescopic Language Model (TLM) to be that continuum: a nested-capacity Transformer supervised by stochastic prefix supervision with a full anchor. items.title: Unifying Distributional Training for One-Step Visual Generation
items.pt: \emph{Distributional training} provides collective supervision for one-step visual generation by matching real and generated features in frozen representation spaces. We introduce \emph{a unified theoretical framework} that separates distribution modeling from matching discrepancy and connects global objectives to pointwise feature updates through Wasserstein gradient flow. items.title: Scaling Long-Form Story Generation via Narrative State Tracking
items.pt: LLMs have demonstrated strong capabilities in creative writing. However, scaling them to full-length novels remains challenging, as maintaining narrative consistency becomes increasingly difficult. Existing story-generation methods typically focus on stories of up to about ten thousand words, leaving their ability to scale to full-length novels underexplored. items.title: TokenCast: Forecasting Token Consumption During LLM Agent Execution
items.pt: When a large language model (LLM) agent executes the same task, token consumption can vary by over an order of magnitude across runs. The agent chooses its next steps based on tool feedback and intermediate results, while the growing context steadily inflates the input size of every subsequent call.
